entries.hypothesis: Invoice-calibrated chars-per-token estimation keeps whole-prompt token estimates within +/-15% of provider-reported input tokens, making refusal-over-truncation safe to enforce (I-C4 / Wave-1 gate A7).
entries.evidence: REFUTED as shipped. The '29.4% -> 0.1%' headline was circular: the benchmark calibrated and measured against the same injected chars-per-token constant, so it measured memorisation, not accuracy. Honest re-measurement (train n=200 -> held-out n=200 per class, per-sample cpt from a realistic within-class distribution, bootstrap 95% CI, B=2000) gives held-out mean |relative error|: english 6.9% [6.2,7.6], code 15.7% [14.2,17.4], cjk 11.5% [10.2,12.9], cyrillic 9.0% [8.1,10.0], json 12.7% [11.4,14.0], mixed 43.9% [42.6,45.2]. EVERY class's p90 exceeds the declared +/-15% (code p90 30.7%, cjk p90 25.4%). Calibration's real win is the class mean: it beats naive chars//4 on cjk (11.5% vs 58.0%), cyrillic (9.0% vs 34.8%) and code (15.7% vs 23.7%), is a wash on english (6.9% vs 7.2%), and is WORSE than naive on bimodal mixed content (43.9% vs 29.2%).
entries.reason: Structural, not a tuning miss: a single scalar cpt per (provider, model) cannot serve heterogeneous content. I-C4 and gate A7 are re-declared distributionally - '+/-15% is a MEAN target for unimodal cells, not a tail guarantee; mixed/bimodal content is a known failure mode'. OLYMPUS_CTX_BUDGET stays default off, so no production path depends on the calibrated estimator.
entries.activation_condition: Turning OLYMPUS_CTX_BUDGET on to drive refusals requires EITHER a per-content-class estimator (cpt keyed by content class, not only by provider/model) OR explicit scoping of enforcement to unimodal cells, with error re-measured on held-out samples that were never used to calibrate.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any held-out class mean |error| above 15% on a cell the flag is enabled for, or mixed-content error exceeding naive chars//4.
entries.cost: $0 today - flag default off, and the estimator is pure local arithmetic. Re-measurement is offline and keyless (seeded corpus, no provider calls).
entries.security_impact: No confidentiality impact. Under-estimation risks an over-full prompt reaching the provider (a visible error, not a silent leak). The poisoning path is separately bounded: out-of-bound/NaN/inf/str/None cpt observations are discarded and the EMA is clamped to [CPT_MIN, CPT_MAX]; flag-off byte-identity was re-confirmed against 1000 histories even with a poisoned calibration file on disk.
entries.outcome: Claim re-declared distributionally rather than withdrawn; capability remains default-off. The shipped benchmark should be relabelled a 'calibration-converges' test, not an accuracy claim.

entries.hypothesis: The replay-fixture secret screen prevents any live credential from reaching a committable fixture (I-R2).
entries.evidence: Blocker B1 found and FIXED: the v1 pattern sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{8,} never engaged on a modern sk-proj-... key, so a live key planted in a frozen response exported into a committable fixture with the manifest reporting a clean scrub. Screen v2 broadened the key shape, added whitespace-tolerant authorization/api-key matching and explicit AWS/GitHub/Slack/Google shapes: all 7 audited vectors are now caught and export REFUSES the smuggled-key fixture (FixtureSecretsError). Residual proven and retained as *_DOCUMENTED_RESIDUAL tests: base64-encoded credentials and secrets split across fields still pass the screen.
entries.reason: Pattern matching cannot see a secret that has been re-encoded or fragmented; catching those needs entropy/structural detection, whose false positives would refuse legitimate high-entropy fixture payloads (hashes, ids, embeddings).
entries.activation_condition: An entropy/structural detector measured on a real fixture corpus with a false-refusal rate low enough to keep `olympus replay --export` usable - target 0 false refusals on the committed fixtures.
entries.deactivation_trigger: A real credential found in any committed fixture: this entry becomes status `incident` and fixture export is disabled until fixed.
entries.cost: $0 - screening is local string work at export time.
entries.security_impact: HIGH class if it fires: a missed credential lands in a committed, shareable artifact. Bounded in practice - the screen covers every plaintext vector seen so far, and the residual requires the producer to deliberately encode or split the secret.
entries.outcome: Blocker fixed (screen v2); the encoding/fragmentation residual is carried as documented debt with the failing vectors kept as tests.

entries.hypothesis: A SHA-256 hash chain is sufficient integrity for the sealed session journal without signing keys or key rotation.
entries.evidence: C1 CONFIRMED by adversarial probes (37 tests): fsync syscall counts measured per durability mode, a record with a valid own seal but a broken prev link caught at the exact boundary and quarantined, concurrent appends with proclock no-op'd demonstrably corrupting the journal (the lock's necessity shown, not assumed), and 9 hostile conversation ids collapsing to a direct child of sessions/. What does NOT exist: any signing or key rotation. Integrity is SHA-256 only, so an attacker who can rewrite the file can also recompute the chain.
entries.reason: Spec section C1.15: `witness.sign_log` is DETACHED, so it layers on later with no journal-format change. Shipping the chain first cost nothing and blocked nothing.
entries.activation_condition: witness.sign_log applied to journal segments under a rotating key, with a test proving a re-sealed tampered journal fails signature verification.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Evidence of an in-place journal rewrite surviving verification in any real deployment.
entries.cost: $0 - local hashing today; signing adds local key operations only.
entries.security_impact: Anyone with write access to MEMORY_DIR can rewrite history and re-seal it undetectably in-file. Mitigated today only by filesystem permissions.

entries.hypothesis: The sealed journal detects every tampering shape, including truncation of committed records.
entries.evidence: C1 fault suite: 12/12 fault classes handled and 0 corrupted records accepted - tamper, reorder, duplicate-seq and version faults are all caught, and a middle-range tombstone's bytes are physically gone after compaction through it. Truncation of a COMMITTED SUFFIX (a rollback to an earlier valid state) is NOT detectable in-file: the surviving prefix is internally consistent and its chain verifies.
entries.reason: Detecting a rollback requires an anchor OUTSIDE the file (a signed high-water mark); spec sections C1.8/C1.15 defer that to the same Wave-2 witness signing work as key rotation.
entries.activation_condition: An external anchor - a witness-signed head sequence/hash stored outside MEMORY_DIR and compared at open - with a test that removing the last N committed records is detected.
entries.deactivation_trigger: A journal rollback observed in operation, or any dispute where the journal is the evidence of record.
entries.cost: $0 - a signed head record per segment.
entries.security_impact: Silent loss of the most recent journal history (for example deleting an incriminating turn) is undetectable from the file alone.

entries.hypothesis: modelgate.classify() assigns the correct drift severity for every shape of change, including a domain that vanishes from a run.
entries.evidence: C6 CONFIRMED after fix: every severity boundary (info/warn_pending/warn/freeze/block/quarantine) verified including the inclusive tolerance edge and the quarantine short-circuit, and reproduce-before-believe holds (an unconfirmed single-domain regression never hardens to warn). Gap: classify() compares SCORED domains only. A domain present in the baseline but MISSING from the new run is ignored rather than treated as a regression.
entries.reason: Narrow in practice - a fully vanished domain usually means provider errors or malformed output, which pushes error_rate over the quarantine threshold first, so the run is already gated. Recorded for Wave-2 severity refinement rather than patched blind.
entries.activation_condition: A severity rule for baseline-present/run-missing domains (treated at that domain's own severity class, so a vanished verify or refusal domain reaches BLOCK), with fixtures for the vanished-domain case.
entries.deactivation_trigger: A real drift run where a domain vanishes without error_rate crossing the quarantine threshold.
entries.cost: $0 - the drift cadence is default off (OLYMPUS_DRIFT_GATE_EVERY=0) and a run is capped by OLYMPUS_DRIFT_BUDGET_USD (default $1.00).
entries.security_impact: A vanished verify/refusal domain is a safety regression that classify() does not escalate to BLOCK on its own today.

entries.hypothesis: I-M1: the drift gate never exceeds its dollar cap (OLYMPUS_DRIFT_BUDGET_USD).
entries.evidence: Blocker B2 found and FIXED. The old projection used the trailing MAX of past per-item costs and was blind to a spike: costs [0.1, 0.1, 5.0] under a $1.00 cap spent $5.20, and 'the first item always runs' let one item exceed the cap unboundedly - I-M1 was FALSE. Replaced by a pre-flight worst-case estimate (an item starts only if total + worst_case(item) <= cap), pricing input + _DRIFT_MAX_OUTPUT (1024) output x _CALLS_PER_ITEM (3) from the same usage.PRICES table. Verified: [0.1, 0.1, 5.0] under $1.00 now stops before the spike (2 items, $0.20) and a single over-cap item runs 0 items at $0; the estimator is injectable so tests assert never-exceed with perfect foresight.
entries.reason: The bound is a true never-exceed bound only while per-item output stays within _DRIFT_MAX_OUTPUT; a provider returning more than that could overrun by a single item's excess. The strictly-safe MAX_TOKENS (16k) bound would block half the 14-item corpus under $1.00, so the tighter realistic bound was chosen deliberately.
entries.activation_condition: A provider-enforced max_tokens on drift calls (so the output bound is enforced rather than assumed), or per-call reconciliation that halts the corpus on the first response exceeding the bound.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any measured drift run whose total spend exceeds OLYMPUS_DRIFT_BUDGET_USD.
entries.cost: Bounded by the cap itself (default $1.00/run); cadence default off, and CI drift/eval tests are keyless with an injected run_fn so no live provider spend occurs.
entries.security_impact: Denial-of-wallet class, now bounded: worst case is one item's excess over the estimate versus the previous unbounded overrun.
entries.outcome: I-M1 restated honestly as 'never-exceed under the short-answer output bound' rather than withdrawn.

entries.hypothesis: Deployments upgrading into the typed tool-call ladder need a one-release escape hatch (OLYMPUS_TOOL_VALIDATE=off) that restores pre-ladder behaviour.
entries.evidence: C8 CONFIRMED at the DEFAULT setting (39 adversarial probes): no repaired or coerced call reaches a handler without passing rung-2 validation against the authoritative input_schema (I-T1); a JSON `true` coerced for an int param stays rejected, so coercion cannot launder a semantically wrong value; unknown tool names are always refused. With OLYMPUS_TOOL_VALIDATE=off that precondition is skipped and the legacy path is measurably less safe.
entries.reason: Intended as a ONE-RELEASE escape hatch for deployments whose tool schemas the ladder rejects; removing it without a release cycle would break them with no warning.
entries.activation_condition: Not applicable - this entry tracks REMOVAL, not enablement. Remove the off path once one full release cycle passes with no deployment reporting a need for it.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any tool call executing unvalidated via the off path in a real deployment: remove the escape hatch immediately.
entries.cost: $0 - a branch, not a call.
entries.security_impact: With the flag off a malformed or semantically wrong tool call can reach a handler - exactly the class the ladder exists to stop. Every other rung's safety argument depends on rung-2 validation being unconditional.

entries.hypothesis: Observability cannot change decisions: a hostile observe-only plugin cannot influence a run, under any dispatch pattern.
entries.evidence: C3 CONFIRMED for the committed fixture: a hostile observe-only plugin mutating pre_llm_call params - including NESTED list mutation - cannot reach the caller (deepcopy, not shallow), and the gate exits 1 on an injected decision diff and 2 on a trivial (<3 decision-type) fixture, so it cannot pass vacuously. Gate run on the shipped fixture is exit 0 (diffs:0, reply_match:true). Gap: the committed mini fixture is SINGLE-THREADED. canonicalize_parallel_since covers ordering, but non-interference under real multi-worker parallel dispatch is UNVERIFIED - not known-broken, unexercised.
entries.reason: A multi-worker replay fixture does not exist yet; building one is Wave-2 integration testing, and the audit refused to claim coverage it had not measured.
entries.activation_condition: A committed multi-worker replay fixture (at least 2 concurrent specialists) that the non-interference gate runs with plugins on and off, yielding 0 decision diffs.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any decision diff observed under parallel dispatch with observability enabled.
entries.cost: $0 - the gate is keyless, offline and under 1 second.
entries.security_impact: If an observability plugin could perturb ordering under parallelism, the audit trail's fidelity claim would be false. Unverified rather than known-broken.

entries.hypothesis: Salvaging a malformed tool call (the ladder's most permissive rung, OLYMPUS_TOOL_SALVAGE) rescues turns that would otherwise fail, without ever executing a semantically wrong call.
entries.evidence: SAFETY CONFIRMED (C8, 42 author tests + 39 adversarial probes): a salvaged call cannot map onto the wrong parameter, and no salvaged call reaches a handler without passing rung-2 schema validation. Ladder overhead measured at 0.016 ms/call against a 0.5 ms target. BENEFIT UNMEASURED: no deployment data yet shows how often salvage actually rescues a real turn.
entries.reason: Shipped default OFF precisely because the safety property is proven and the value is not - an opt-in experiment, not a default.
entries.activation_condition: Enable where repair_stats shows salvage rescuing real turns; a deployment with a 0% salvage-success rate should turn it off. Promotion to default-on requires a measured rescue rate.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any salvaged call executing with wrong parameters, or a rising repair rate that indicates provider decay rather than recoverable noise (OLYMPUS_REPAIR_WARN_RATE).
entries.cost: 0.016 ms/call; no provider calls.
entries.security_impact: The most permissive rung; safe only because rung-2 schema validation is unconditional. If OLYMPUS_TOOL_VALIDATE=off (see toolcall-validate-off-legacy) that guarantee is gone and salvage must not be enabled.
entries.outcome: Safety CONFIRMED by independent audit; benefit still unmeasured, so it stays opt-in.

entries.hypothesis: Preferring the pool member with the best RECORDED success rate (Wilson lower bound over routing_outcomes) beats the keyword heuristic, and is never worse where evidence is thin.
entries.evidence: The never-worse half is enforced in code, not assumed: activation requires the operator opt-in (default OFF), NOT replaying, the SPEC-04 Phase B data gate (enough labeled, non-synthetic outcomes across enough task types), and per-decision evidence for BOTH the challenger and the incumbent cell - no override on one-sided data. With no data it never engages, so it falls back to the heuristic byte-for-byte. NOT measured: whether it is actually BETTER in production. No A/B has been run.
entries.reason: Fallback discipline is proven; the benefit claim is not, so it stays opt-in and evidence-gated rather than becoming a default.
entries.activation_condition: Enable only where routing_outcomes clears the Phase B gate. Promotion to default-on requires an A/B showing a quality or cost win, which does not exist.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any override of the heuristic on one-sided evidence, any engagement during replay, or a measured quality regression versus the heuristic.
entries.cost: $0 - ledger reads only; no extra provider calls.
entries.security_impact: A poisoned outcome ledger would steer routing. Outcomes are labeled from real runs and gated on non-synthetic sources, and sovereign mode filters the pool BEFORE selection, so it can only choose among already-eligible members.

entries.hypothesis: UCB1 exploration over the same routing_outcomes ledger discovers a better model that the conservative exploiter never tries, at a bounded exploration cost.
entries.evidence: Replay-safety is structural: selection is argmax over counts (UCB1), NOT Thompson sampling, so the same ledger always yields the same pick, and it is forced off during replay anyway. A MIN_WARMUP of recorded outcomes per specialist prevents cold-start picks. NOT measured: regret - the turns spent on a worse model have never been quantified against the exploitation win.
entries.reason: Mutually exclusive with learned-routing (an operator runs one or the other); shipping either default-on would create a second selector, which synthesis ruling R1 forbids.
entries.activation_condition: Enable only with an explicit exploration budget in mind. Promotion requires measured regret on real traffic (exploration cost versus discovered win).
entries.deactivation_trigger: Exploration cost exceeding the measured win, or any engagement during replay.
entries.cost: Real: exploration deliberately spends turns on under-sampled models. The amount is unquantified, which is why it is off by default.
entries.security_impact: Same ledger-poisoning surface as learned-routing; deterministic selection means a poisoned ledger steers reproducibly rather than randomly, which makes the effect auditable.

entries.hypothesis: Embedding-based specialist matching routes tasks the keyword router misses, without making any specialist unreachable.
entries.evidence: Safety by construction: opt-in (default OFF), engages only where an embedding backend exists, and degrades to the keyword router, so no specialist becomes unroutable. NOT measured: routing accuracy versus the keyword router on real traffic.
entries.reason: An adaptive selection surface whose benefit claim has never been measured - exactly the kind of feature this registry exists to keep from drifting into 'default because nobody re-checked'.
entries.activation_condition: Enable where an embedding backend is configured. Promotion requires a measured routing-accuracy win over the keyword router on labeled tasks.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any specialist becoming unreachable, or a measured routing-accuracy regression versus the keyword router.
entries.cost: One embedding lookup per routed task where a backend is configured; no council model calls.
entries.security_impact: Task text reaches the embedding backend - an egress consideration on deployments using a remote embedder.

entries.hypothesis: Scoping a specialist's in-prompt skill index to the top-K most relevant skills keeps a large library usable without making any skill unreachable.
entries.evidence: Shipped as the DEFERRED #3 closure: it engages only once a library outgrows the prompt, is replay-frozen per specialist, and degrades to the FULL index, so the failure mode is 'no better than before' rather than 'a skill disappears'. Default ON with OLYMPUS_SEMANTIC_SKILLS=off as the kill switch. NOT measured: top-K recall - whether the scoped index actually contains the skill the task needed.
entries.reason: Default-on is justified by the fallback, not by a measured retrieval win; registered here so the unmeasured half stays visible.
entries.activation_condition: Already on. A measured top-K recall figure on real tasks is what would close this entry rather than keep it under review.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any skill provably unreachable in a live prompt, or replay divergence in the scoped index.
entries.cost: Embedding lookups against an existing index; no additional council model calls.
entries.security_impact: None beyond the embedding store's existing scope; per-specialist freezing keeps replay deterministic.

entries.hypothesis: Measured usefulness (retrieval -> verifier acceptance, reuse, avoided cost/latency) predicts which context and skill items are worth pinning better than raw frequency does, and a heat-driven pin set beats static placement on a before/after benchmark.
entries.evidence: NONE - no swap telemetry has been collected. The hysteresis and decay constants in the proposed ctxheat design are PROVISIONAL: inherited shapes, not values derived from Olympus data. The Wave-1 audit directive forbids shipping uncalibrated inherited constants as live policy.
entries.reason: Wave-2 universal rule: no uncalibrated inherited constants. Until the constants come from real swap telemetry, ctxheat may only run in SHADOW mode - recording heat and PROPOSING pin sets while changing nothing.
entries.activation_condition: OLYMPUS_CTXHEAT=on requires BOTH: hysteresis/decay constants derived from recorded swap telemetry (calibration owner named in the module), AND a passing before/after pin-set benchmark gate - the same discipline gate_prompt already applies (W2-I2.4).
entries.deactivation_trigger: Benchmark-gate regression, the pin budget being exceeded, or any raw user content found in a heat ledger (a W2-I2.1 content-minimisation violation).
entries.cost: Shadow mode: ledger writes only (ids, counters, scores, timestamps, provenance). No model calls and no new heartbeat cadence.
entries.security_impact: Heat poisoning - an injected item farming its own promotion - is the designed threat. Mitigations: only gated-store content is eligible, usefulness requires VERIFIER acceptance which the injecting path cannot grant itself, and per-user ledgers are isolated.

entries.hypothesis: One measured evidence store keyed by member x task cell can answer 'is this model qualified for THIS kind of task?' well enough to replace hand-typed capability claims in routing.
entries.evidence: NONE - the store does not exist. Today's inputs are the hand-typed config._CAPABILITIES table plus raw routing_outcomes counts, modelgate drift rows and evals baselines: none of them qualify a model per task cell, so a model can currently be selected on a human-written claim alone.
entries.reason: Wave-2 C1 and synthesis ruling R1 (one ladder, not three selectors). Ships default off until cards accumulate real observations; W2-I1.1 means a _CAPABILITIES entry may seed a PRIOR but can never yield `qualified`.
entries.activation_condition: OLYMPUS_MODELGRADE=on requires cards with n >= MIN_N, a Wilson lower bound at or above the cell's floor, freshness within OLYMPUS_GRADE_TTL_DAYS, and no freeze/quarantine from modelgate for that key.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any promotion traceable to a manual claim rather than measured evidence (W2-I1.1 violation), or a routing quality regression attributable to a card.
entries.cost: Reads existing evidence stores; observations ride runs that already happen, so no new provider calls and no new cadence.
entries.security_impact: Evidence poisoning is the designed threat: observations are bounds-validated, append-only and fully keyed, and scores derive from verifier/eval outcomes - never from a model's self-report, so a compromised provider cannot inflate its own grade.

entries.hypothesis: A cheaper or warmer qualified candidate can be substituted inside a measured quality band with no user-visible quality loss, at a measurable cost saving.
entries.evidence: NONE - and it cannot be gathered yet: the prerequisite (modelgrade cards) does not exist, so no substitution can currently be justified by measured evidence.
entries.reason: Ships off. Shadow mode records the counterfactual - which substitution it WOULD have made, plus agreement telemetry - without changing any routing decision.
entries.activation_condition: OLYMPUS_ROUTESUB=on requires ALL of: both candidates qualified for the cell in modelgrade, the cheaper candidate above the cell's minimum quality floor, the verifier floor preserved, security classification permitting, context/tool requirements supported, fresh evidence, and a shadow-mode agreement record showing no quality loss.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any substitution below Aletheia's measured verification floor (W2-I3.1, a hard test-enforced rule), any undisclosed user-visible degradation (W2-I3.2), or agreement telemetry showing quality erosion.
entries.cost: Intended to REDUCE spend. Shadow mode costs one telemetry row per routing decision and nothing else.
entries.security_impact: Cost-driven quality erosion is the threat; quality floors, the verifier floor and mandatory disclosure are the mitigations. A cheaper model is never automatically permitted on a security-classified cell.

entries.hypothesis: Useful progress (completed plan nodes, validated tool results, accepted specialist output) detects stalls and runaway spend that liveness checks miss, at an acceptable false-positive rate.
entries.evidence: NONE - the module does not exist. Today a progress-free but 'live' run (retry loop, repeated identical calls, runaway tool recursion) is bounded only by OLYMPUS_RUN_BUDGET_USD, i.e. after the money is spent.
entries.reason: Ships off; observe mode records what it WOULD cancel. W2-I6.1: model-generated text alone is NEVER proof of progress, so token flow cannot be used as the liveness signal.
entries.activation_condition: OLYMPUS_WATCHDOG=enforce requires a measured false-positive rate on real traffic below the acceptance gate - a slow-but-progressing run must never be cancelled.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any cancellation of a run that was making genuine progress, or forensic state lost on cancellation.
entries.cost: Observation only: lease bookkeeping on events that already occur. No new heartbeat cadence and no provider calls.
entries.security_impact: Denial-of-wallet defence - progress-free spend is stopped and admission slots released. A false positive is an availability risk, which is exactly why enforce mode is gated on a measured FP rate.

entries.hypothesis: Draft-cheap/verify-strong speculation cuts latency and cost on cells where a cheap draft is usually accepted, without anchoring the verifier to the draft.
entries.evidence: NONE. There is no per-cell acceptance data anywhere in the tree, and the qualification input (modelgrade cards) does not exist either.
entries.reason: Explicitly excluded from Wave 2. Building it before per-cell acceptance data exists would mean inventing the acceptance thresholds - the inherited-constant failure the Wave-1 audit forbids.
entries.activation_condition: Wave 3, gated on: modelgrade cards qualifying BOTH a draft and a verify model for the cell, plus a per-cell A/B showing the acceptance rate pays for the second call, with per-cell auto-disable on acceptance decay.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Anti-anchoring test failure (the verifier agreeing with a wrong draft above chance) or per-cell acceptance below break-even.
entries.cost: Speculation spends two calls to save one - a NET LOSS wherever acceptance is low, which is the whole reason it is evidence-gated.
entries.security_impact: A draft model influencing a verification outcome would break epistemic independence; the anti-anchoring rejection rule is the mitigation and must be tested, not assumed.

entries.hypothesis: Coupling tables built from real trajectories predict the next step well enough that staging-only prefetch pays for itself.
entries.evidence: Measured and NOT met. coupling.predictability_report() writes NOTHING (filesystem snapshot before/after identical) and the audit confirmed no OLYMPUS_PREFETCH consumer exists anywhere in olympus/. The floors abstain below n and require n >= 200; no report has qualified.
entries.reason: Ruling R5 / domain 08: predictability is a go/no-go gate BEFORE any prefetch is built. The report exists so the decision is made on data rather than on the appeal of the idea.
entries.activation_condition: The predictability floor: recall@2 >= 0.6 with Wilson-CI half-width <= 0.1 on n >= 200 for at least one predictor, measured on real trajectories. Even then prefetch stays staging-only with a $0 default budget.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Floors dropping below threshold on fresh data, or any network call attributable to prefetch.
entries.cost: $0 today - report only, no consumer. A future consumer carries a budget that defaults to $0.
entries.security_impact: Speculative fetching would act on unverified predictions; staging-only with a $0 budget bounds both the spend and the egress.
entries.outcome: Floors NOT met; prefetch remains unbuilt. The report's read-only property was independently re-verified in the Wave-1 audit.

entries.hypothesis: A locally-hosted model can be QUALIFIED - not assumed - for specific low-risk task cells, cutting cost and keeping data local.
entries.evidence: NONE - no qualification campaign has been run and no local-model evidence exists in any store.
entries.reason: Wave 3, and it needs modelgrade first (R1: one ladder). A local model is qualified by exactly the same measured evidence as a hosted one - sovereignty is not an exemption from the floors.
entries.activation_condition: modelgrade cards showing the local model qualified for the specific cells (n >= MIN_N, Wilson lower bound at or above the cell floor, evidence fresh). Also budget-gated: Wave 3 has ZERO module headroom under the 14-module cap, so this must fit one of the 3 approved slots.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Any local model routed to a cell it is not qualified for, or measured quality below that cell's floor.
entries.cost: Local inference is a hardware cost rather than per-token; the qualification campaign itself costs eval runs against the measurement budget.
entries.security_impact: Positive intent (data stays local) but a weaker model on a security-relevant cell is a real risk. What permits it is the qualification floor, never the sovereignty argument.

entries.hypothesis: Deterministic provider mirroring with health probes improves availability without breaking replay determinism or epistemic independence.
entries.evidence: NONE. Today there is one provider path per pool member; failover is key rotation WITHIN a provider (429/402/insufficient balance), not cross-provider mirroring, and no provider-unavailability rate has been measured to justify more.
entries.reason: Wave 3. Mirroring interacts with singleflight dedup and with Aletheia's fresh=True independence requirement, so it cannot be bolted on ad hoc without breaking one of them.
entries.activation_condition: Wave 3, gated on: a measured provider-unavailability rate worth mitigating, deterministic mirror selection (replay reproduces the recorded provider), and dedup scoping that never shares a cached result across a trust boundary or into Aletheia.
entries.deactivation_trigger: Replay divergence caused by mirror selection, or any deduped result crossing a trust boundary.
entries.cost: Health probes are a NEW cadence and must register in the single heartbeat table under OLYMPUS_MEASURE_BUDGET_USD (budget rule B2) - no cadence self-adds.
entries.security_impact: Mirroring sends the same prompt to a second provider: an egress and data-residency decision that must be explicit, never a silent failover side effect.
